Vs.

full_judgment: Mr B Hossain, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the Government-petitioner, submits that the High Court Division failed to reverse the trial Court's definite finding that the suit was not maintainable in law, that it was bad for defect of parties and that the suit has been undervalued and proper Court fees have not been paid thereon. He further submits that the prescribed authority (the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar) did not act on any application submitted by the plaintiff within 3 months of the promulgation of PO No. 16 of 1972. He acted on an application filed by the plaintiff on 16-3-1982, i.e., 10 years after the prescribed period and, as such, the proceeding taken by the prescribed authority was itself without jurisdiction and void ab initio which the High Court Division failed to consider. He further submits that there is no reversal of the finding of the trial Court that Syed Mahbubur Rahman was not present in Bangladesh ever since the liberation of the country. He further submits that the plaintiff cannot get the relief as prayed for in the plaint upon a mere agreement for sale and cannot zet restoration of possession in any case, which the High Court Division failed to consider. He also submits that the High Court Division erred in law and in the facts, circumstances and evidence of the case that the suit property was not an abandoned property.
